purpose: Teach: 待望/見慣れ/あいにく/小麦/大まか/風習/嘆き/気まぐれ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、待望の長男が生まれたぞ
lines.en: Your grandmother — when I was young, the long-awaited firstborn arrived.
lines.style: Gentle, reaching back into memory. Opening word soft but grounded. Pace unhurried, like handling something fragile. The dates matter to him; he lingers on the turning points.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、見慣れた村の景色を懐かしまれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes — you remember the familiar fields and that old village sky, don't you, dear?
lines.style: Warm recognition, almost teasing in its certainty. She's confirming what she already knows he's feeling. Slight upturn at the end — invitation rather than question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、あいにくの雨で結婚式が延期になったぞ
lines.en: And then — the rain came on our wedding day. We had to postpone.
lines.style: Quiet resignation mixed with acceptance. The word 'rain' lands with light weight — not a complaint, just fact. Trailing off slightly, as if he's moved past the disappointment decades ago.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、小麦粉でうどんを打たれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But you made udon from scratch that day, didn't you? With your own hands.
lines.style: Soft wonder. She's looking at him, not at the memory. The admiration is real and unsurprised — she knew who he was even then. Slight emphasis on 'your own hands.'

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、村の予定が大まかに決まってたぞ
lines.en: Life in the village — everything was planned out, more or less. That was how it was.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact but gentle. He's stating a condition, not complaining. Slight pause before 'that was how it was' — acknowledging the weight and inevitability of it all.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、村の風習を大切にされたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you held to those customs so carefully. You still do, even now.
lines.style: Steadying, almost protective in tone. She's affirming something foundational about him. Warm but serious — this matters to her. No rush in the delivery.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、戦争の嘆きを語る人が多かったぞ
lines.en: Many people spoke of war then. The sadness — everyone carried it.
lines.style: Low, respectful weight. His voice doesn't rise. He's honoring something, and the pace slows. 'Everyone carried it' trails just slightly, acknowledging the burden they all shared.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、気まぐれにお花を摘んでくださったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: But sometimes you'd stop what you were doing and pick wildflowers for me. Just like that.
lines.style: Voice softens further. Almost whispers the image into being. 'Just like that' — a small gesture, but she's saying it held everything. Breath gentle, trailing off with quiet awe.
